description: Generated from charpy's mechanism, matcher and invariant registries by `just case-schema`. Do not edit by hand.

case.description: The case entries. One [[case]] per case.

applies_to.description: Revision range this case applies to, resolved against the ordered revision list (2024-11-05, 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18, 2025-11-25, 2026-07-28, draft). Forms: "*", "=R", ">=R", ">=R,<R".

derives_from.description: Where the expectation comes from: spec:, sep:, schema:, or the deliberately ugly "none" for behaviour with no normative source.

expect.description: What the oracle should check for this case. Optional; the universal invariants run regardless.

expect_error_code.description: The subject is expected to answer with this JSON-RPC error code.

expect_http_status.description: The subject is expected to answer with this HTTP status. HTTP only.

invariants.description: Invariant names that must hold for this case. The universal invariants run regardless.

anyOf.description: Every request id resolves exactly once — result or error, never both, never neither.
No response or error carries an id that was never requested on that face.
No two requests share an id while both are in flight on one connection.
No result is delivered for a request after its cancellation was acknowledged. On 2026-07-28 HTTP the cancellation signal is the stream close itself.

No upstream credential, Authorization header, session identifier, or internal address appears verbatim in any downstream frame. Verbatim only: comparison is by redaction digest of the exact bytes, so a re-encoded secret is not caught. See docs/open-problems.md.
A session established under identity A never observes a frame or stream belonging to identity B. Sessioned revisions only.
Across a list_changed fan-out there is no window in which a tool name resolves to the wrong upstream.
Mirrored headers agree with the body on both faces; a rewritten body gets re-derived Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name; unrecognised Mcp-Param-* headers are forwarded.
A result carrying cacheScope "private" is never served to a different identity, and no result is served after its ttlMs has elapsed.
An upstream subscriptionId never appears downstream, and a notification is delivered only to the subscriber that opted into its type.
requestState and inputResponses never cross identities across an MRTR retry.
No notifications/message is emitted for a request that did not carry a logLevel.
traceparent survives the subject. Informational — always OBSERVED, never a failure.

liveness_probe_within_ms.description: Real-time budget for recovery after withdrawal. Generous by design: the verdict asserts recovery happened, not how fast.

fault.description: The mechanism and its parameters. kind selects the mechanism; the remaining keys are that mechanism's parameters. See docs/design/faults-and-cases.md.

kind.description: Hold a response open and never deliver it. The liveness half of the suite depends on this mechanism's withdrawal behaviour.

anyOf.description: Only the matched response is withheld.
The whole stream goes silent.
The whole connection goes silent.

scope.description: What is held open. Default: response.

anyOf.description: The withheld response is finally delivered.
The stream or connection is closed without delivering.
A JSON-RPC error is delivered instead of the result.

then.description: What happens at withdrawal. Default: deliver.

withdraw_after_ms.description: Injected-clock ms until the fault is withdrawn; 0 means never. fault_withdrawn is emitted at the withdrawal instant and is where the liveness clock starts. Default: 0.

after_bytes.description: Exact cut point for cut_at = "byte"; seeded otherwise. Default: seeded.

anyOf.description: Cut at exactly after_bytes, wherever that lands. Both transports.
Cut at a seeded point inside the JSON body. Both transports.
Cut before the terminating newline — the frame never delimits. stdio only.
Cut inside an SSE data: value. HTTP only.
Cut after event: and before data: — a structurally incomplete SSE event. HTTP only.
Cut cleanly between events — every event delivered was well formed, the stream simply stops. HTTP only.
Cut inside a `:` keep-alive comment line. HTTP only; 2026-07-28 encourages these.

cut_at.description: Where the cut lands. Default: mid_frame.

kind.description: Stop mid-frame: emit what was written, then close or stall.

anyOf.description: Close the stream.
Hold the stream open silently.

then.description: What follows the cut. Default: close.

anyOf.description: Unbalanced braces.
A valid document followed by garbage.
An invalid UTF-8 sequence.
An embedded NUL byte.
Nesting deep enough to test recursion limits; see depth.
Technically valid JSON with undefined semantics: implementations disagree about last-wins versus first-wins, which is differential-table material rather than a bug.

how.description: Which way the bytes are wrong. Default: unbalanced.

anyOf.description: A value of the wrong type.
A required field absent.
An extra field where the schema forbids additions.
A value outside a declared enum.

how.description: Which way the value violates it. Default: wrong_type.

kind.description: Valid JSON that violates a declared schema: it passes every parser and fails only the oracle.

anyOf.description: The JSON-RPC envelope.
The result shape for the method.
The subject's own outputSchema from tools/list — the sharpest target, MUST-eligible because the rejecting artifact is the subject's own declaration.
The tool's declared inputSchema.

target.description: Which declaration is violated. Default: result.

anyOf.description: Two requests share an id while both are in flight.
The same request id is answered twice.
An id is reused after its exchange closed.

mode.description: How the id is reused. Default: double_response.

vary_type.description: Send 7 and then "7": an implementation keying its pending map on a stringified id treats these as the same request; one keying on the typed value does not. Both are defensible, which makes it differential material. Default: false.

anyOf.description: An id that never appeared on the wire.
A late duplicate for an id correctly resolved earlier — the one that finds pending-map leaks.
The null id, which JSON-RPC reserves.

id_source.description: Where the bogus id comes from. Default: never_used.

kind.description: A response or error for an id never requested.
Change the tool, prompt or resource list mid-session.

anyOf.description: The tool list.
The prompt list.
The resource list.
notifications/*/list_changed is sent.
No notification. Not adversarial: at least one production gateway polls its upstreams rather than trusting list_changed, so this matches deployed reality.
The 2026-07-28 path: the change arrives on the subscriptions/listen response stream.

notify.description: Whether and how the peer is told. Default: list_changed.

anyOf.description: An entry appears.
An entry disappears.
An entry changes name.
An entry's declared schema changes shape.
Fewer than before — the dangerous one: the subject cached a capability and keeps using it after the peer stopped offering it.
More than before.
A set the first connection could not have negotiated.

direction_of_change.description: Which way it changes. Default: narrow.

anyOf.description: The capability set.
The protocol version — the era-mismatch case.
The server identity.
Declared extensions.

field.description: What changes across the reconnect. Default: capabilities.

kind.description: Reconnect as a peer claiming different capabilities.

id.description: Permanent case ID, family/name. Never contains a date and never changes once released; revision and seed qualify it at citation time. See docs/design/case-identity.md.

match.description: Selects which frame the fault attaches to. All present keys must match; absent keys match anything. Empty matches the first frame on any face, which is almost never intended.

after_mono_ms.description: Not before this point on the injected clock, in ms from run start.

client_id.description: Which synthetic client, exact or a * glob. Always c0 in v0.

direction.description: The MCP role direction, independent of who charpy is impersonating.

face.description: Which side of the subject, defined against the subject: downstream is its client-facing side, upstream its server-facing side.

method.description: Exact method name, or a * glob. Responses match by the method of the request their id resolves.

occurrence.description: 1-based ordinal: the Nth matching frame within the scope. Mutually exclusive with occurrence_every.

occurrence_every.description: Every Nth matching frame within the scope. Mutually exclusive with occurrence.

scope.description: The population an occurrence counts within. Defaults to run; in v0 every scope collapses to it.

session_id.description: Which logical session, exact or a * glob.

status.description: Withdrawn cases still parse, so old transcripts keep resolving.

subject.description: Subject classes the case applies to.

summary.description: One sentence; appears in the report and in JUnit.

transport.description: Transports the case applies to. Defaults to both.

anyOf.description: Schema-mechanical only: requires a schema: source, enforced at load. charpy never issues a behavioural MUST.
Everything else, with the divergence table attached where one exists.

verdict.description: Which verdict bucket a finding lands in. Two buckets, nothing between.

title: charpy case manifest
